newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM sees progress with Pakistan in some areas.
newsitem.headline: India PM sees progress with Pakistan in some areas.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral has written to his Pakistani counterpart saying he was confident the two neighbours could reach agreement in many areas during bilateral talks despite differences on some issues.

"Though we may not agree on all issues, we see a wide range of subjects on which we believe we can collaborate effectively," Gujral said in a letter to Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif that the Foreign Ministry released on Thursday.
"I trust that our bilateral talks will help to expand cooperation in mutually beneficial areas."
Gujral was responding to a congratulatory message which Sharif sent to him on Tuesday after the new Indian leader had won a vote of confidence in parliament.
Sharif said the selection of Gujral had boosted hopes for peace between their two countries.

Last month, senior civil servants in the two countries' foreign ministries held the first high-level bilateral talks between the longtime foes in three years. Both countries said they were willing to discuss all outstanding differences.
Gujral, who was foreign minister in ousted prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government, then met Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan in New Delhi on April 9.
Negotiations had broken down in 1994 over Kashmir, which is divided between the two nations and was the cause of two of the three wars that Pakistan and India have fought since independence in 1947.

Islamabad, which stakes a claim to all of Kashmir, had insisted that the two countries narrow differences over the Himalayan region before tackling other issues. India was ready to address less contentious issues simultaneously.
Sharif alluded to the thorny issue of Kashmir in his message to Gujral.

"The success of our efforts will naturally depend on the seriousness of purpose and political 'will' with which the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir is addressed," he said, referring to the northern Indian state which includes two thirds of Kashmir.
Gujral, who has retained the foreign ministry portfolio, said he was glad that after a long break, the two countries had recently revived bilateral talks on all outstanding issues.
"With each of us showing a constructive and forward-looking approach, we are confident that our exchanges will be useful and lead to mutually beneficial results," Gujral said.
"I am determined not to spare any effort in this endeavour."
The new Indian prime minister said he looked forward to meeting Sharif in the Maldives next month to renew the personal contact which they established in Islamabad some years ago.
The two leaders are expected to meet on the fringes of a summit meeting of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) in the Maldives scheduled for May 12 to 14.
The two countries' foreign secretaries may meet in Islamabad before the regional summit.
